[LREG.4.1] The binding form for a capture-bearing match is a parenthesised,
comma-separated, positional list of identifiers, and it attaches to a
**`where` clause**. An ordinary predicate may follow it on the same clause, and
may reference the captures ([LGRA.8.1]).

**The capture form is a `where` form, and only a `where` form.** A capture must
not be written as a `let`: a `let` is RHS-only ([LLET]), so it is evaluated
after the rule has fired, and there is no answer to what a capture is worth when
the pattern did not match.

**In `where`, the question does not arise.** A non-matching pattern is a pattern
that does not match: no activation is created, and there is no binding to give a
value to. That is why [LREG.4.4] can say the captured values are `String` rather
than `String?`.
